Omar N: Hey everyone, joining from a Surface Laptop (Windows 11) using WSL2 Ubuntu. Trying to follow the mac-focused dotfiles bootstrap and hit a bunch of weird errors: asdf plugins install fine but `asdf install python 3.11.6` fails with "configure: error: OpenSSL library not found". Also `asdf install nodejs 20.1.0` bombs with the GPG import step (gpg: can't connect to the agent). Any WSL-specific tips?

Tess Y: Welcome Omar! For OpenSSL on WSL make sure the distro has the dev packages: `sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y build-essential libssl-dev zlib1g-dev libbz2-dev libreadline-dev libsqlite3-dev libncursesw5-dev libgdbm-dev liblzma-dev`. pyenv/asdf need those.

Omar N: I installed those but python build still says ssl module missing. I also noticed `~/.asdf/plugins/python/bin/install` tries to use `pkg-config --libs openssl` but pkg-config isn't returning anything.

Ben R: Install `pkg-config` and point to the right OpenSSL: on Ubuntu 22.04 OpenSSL 3 is default, so `sudo apt install pkg-config libssl-dev` should fix pkg-config outputs. If you built OpenSSL from source earlier, remove conflicting libs.

Omar N: Great, that fixed python. For the node GPG issue I think gpg agent isn't available in WSL. The error is `gpg: signing failed: No agent`.

Tess Y: For gpg in WSL you can either run gpg-agent inside WSL or use a Windows gpg agent via wslgnupg. Quick fix: install gnupg2 and pinentry: `sudo apt install gnupg2 pinentry-curses`, then export `GPG_TTY=$(tty)` and start `gpg-agent --daemon`. Or use `wsl --shutdown` then restart if you just installed packages.

Omar N: I installed pinentry and started gpg-agent, the import-release-team-keyring script progressed further but then failed at fetching keys from hkps://keys.openpgp.org. Network seems flaky behind our corporate proxy.

Ben R: If behind a proxy, set `export http_proxy=http://proxy.company:3128` and `export https_proxy=http://proxy.company:3128` in your shell before running gpg/wget/curl. For a one-off you can download the key on Windows and copy it into WSL (`/mnt/c/Users/<you>/Downloads`).

Omar N: Thanks. Last WSL oddity: direnv hooks in fish aren't loading; my `~/.config/fish/config.fish` has `source ~/.asdf/asdf.fish` and `eval (direnv hook fish)` like the mac docs but `direnv allow` still errors with "layout asdf: plugin not found"

Tess Y: Check that asdf installs plugins under `~/.asdf/plugins/nodejs` etc. If plugin exists but layout still fails, ensure the repo .envrc is using the correct plugin name: we use `use asdf` in some repos and `layout asdf` in others depending on plugin version. For fish you might need `eval (asdf where nodejs >/dev/null; and direnv export fish)` hack but better to update `.envrc` to `use asdf` which is more explicit: e.g., `use asdf nodejs 20.1.0`

Omar N: Ah `use asdf` worked. Two final questions: 1) Do we recommend setting environment vars like `GOPATH` / `RUSTFLAGS` globally in WSL or per-project? 2) Who do I ping for syncing dotfiles and 1Password SSH key access?

Ben R: 1) Keep them per-project in `.envrc` to avoid leaking build-time flags. For GOPATH you can set `export GOPATH=$HOME/go` in your shell rc if you prefer global, but we usually rely on modules so it's optional. For RUSTFLAGS put them in `.envrc` when needed. 2) Ping the #new-hires channel and tag `@ops` or DM me. I'll open a ticket to add you to `redwood/new-hires/ssh` in 1Password.

infra-bot: Created ticket OPS-2289 to add Omar N to 1Password 'redwood/new-hires/ssh' and assigned to @Ben R. :robot_face:

Omar N: Awesome, thanks Tess and Ben 389 I'll tidy my .envrc and report back if anything else breaks.
